scope: Read-only reuse and source-to-source comparison of the 2026-10-16 headed API experiment, V171 shipping factory, and V168/V169 production failures. No test rerun, build, app launch, profile change, signature, or publication.

reusedRuntimeEvidence.environment: macOS 27.0, arm64, system WKWebView in a Swift test process; two fresh nonpersistent stores; one visible window.
reusedRuntimeEvidence.observation: The random .invalid named page loaded the fixture proxy response with 2 accepted connections, 1 authenticated upstream and zero direct-origin arrivals. The fixture used an empty matchDomains list, failover disabled, no excluded domains, HTTP CONNECT and test credentials.
reusedRuntimeEvidence.separateNegative: A later local RFC1918 target was reached directly before and after proxy revocation. This remains a concrete Direct-bypass FAIL for that local-address scope.

configurationComparison.matchSelector: Same empty selector state at the NWProxyConfig/API-object level.
configurationComparison.endpointDifference: The experiment proxy listener was bound to the Mac private interface address. The shipping broker endpoint is 127.0.0.1; the prior PASS does not qualify loopback-endpoint selection.
configurationComparison.sourceVersionDifference: The historical test source hash differs from the current source. The result is reused only as a bounded same-OS API behavior observation, not byte-bound product evidence.

updatedInterpretation: The earlier statement that empty-list proxy selection has no runtime evidence was too broad: one named .invalid request passed through an empty-match system-WebKit configuration. Apple documentation still does not establish all-host semantics, and this test does not qualify the owned WebKit host, production factory endpoint, persistent profile lifecycle, or a general no-direct-fallback guarantee. The build-200 no-window/no-CONNECT result therefore cannot be attributed to the empty selector alone.
limitations: No owned WebKit runtime or exact build-200 package was tested.
The proxy endpoint differed from the shipping loopback broker.
Only one named HTTP synthetic origin passed; HTTPS, DNS and external sites were not covered.
The same historical run detected Direct bypass for a local RFC1918 destination.
No release or anonymity claim follows.
nextAction: Do not repeat the historical Direct WebKit or build-200 attempt. When a changed candidate can be secure-timestamp signed, use one run with child-startup, visible-window, navigation, loopback-broker and direct-origin counters so the current no-CONNECT boundary is observable.
